results.content: (2020b) demonstrate that architectural choices in multilingual MT impact the systems’ behavior: Shared encoder-decoders retain less gender information in the source embeddings and less diversion in the attention than language-specific encoder-decoders (Escolano et al., 2021), thus disfavoring the generation of feminine forms. First accounts on gender bias in MT date back to Frank et al. **Beyond Dichotomies.** Besides a few notable exceptions for English NLP tasks (Manzini et al., 2019; Cao and Daumé III, 2020; Sun et al., 2021) and one in MT (Saunders et al., 2020), the discussion around gender bias has been reduced to the binary masculine/feminine dichotomy.
